problem_statement: Applications that parse command-line arguments using the kernel/libc getopt_long() or getopt_long_only() interfaces can observe incorrect parsing when an unrecognized long option is present, especially when it is the final argv entry. A caller that repeatedly invokes the parser until the end-of-options return value is reached can continue receiving the invalid-option return value after the command-line arguments have been exhausted, causing the caller to perform many more iterations than there are arguments in argv and potentially preventing normal termination of the parsing loop. The problem can occur with both the long-option form and the getopt_long_only() dash-style option syntax. The expected behavior is that an unrecognized long option is reported once as invalid and is not repeatedly reprocessed; when it is the final argument, the next parser call should return the end-of-options value. Recognized options, and long options that are rejected for reasons other than being wholly unsupported, should continue to behave normally.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: When getopt_long()/getopt_long_only() encounter an unrecognized long option (e.g. --OptionX), the parser fails to skip over that argv[] entry: optind is not advanced and optptr is left pointing into the unrecognized option. As a result a command line ending in an invalid long option misbehaves (optind stays un-advanced / option count is wrong), producing an ERROR in the ostest getopt() tests. The fix must cause an unrecognized long option to be skipped (advance optind and clear optptr) so that parsing of the remaining options proceeds and the option count/optind checks pass.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The OS test fails when the updated testing/ostest/getopt.c changes are applied. The updated test exercises getopt(), getopt_long(), and getopt_long_only() with new cases in which the last command-line argument is an unsupported long option. It also sets the final argv entry to NULL and calls the test helpers expecting only five option-processing results, and it updates the optind range checks so that optind may point at the NULL argv entry after the last argument. On the unmodified implementation, running ostest produces: ERROR: ndx=12 (expected 5) | ERROR: ndx=12 (expected 5) | ostest_main: Exiting with status 0 | run_tests: ERROR in output | run_tests: result=1. The problem is triggered when a command line contains a long option that is not recognized by the long option table, especially when that unrecognized long option is the final option. The test observes an unexpected number of option-processing iterations and/or an incorrect optind result instead of the expected count. The required behavior is that an unrecognized long option is reported once as an error but is treated as a single command-line argument, so option processing does not keep acting as though more options are present at that same argument. When the unrecognized long option is the final argument, subsequent processing should terminate normally and optind may point at the NULL argv entry. With that behavior, the updated getopt_test must pass.
